statement: A circle passes through $(0,0)$, $(6,0)$ and $(0,8)$. (i) Find its centre and radius. (ii) Find the equation of the tangent to the circle at $(0,8)$. (iii) Find where this tangent meets the x-axis. (iv) Show that the point $(6,8)$ also lies on the circle.
solution: (i) Let the circle be $x^{2}+y^{2}+ux+vy=0$ (since it passes through the origin). From $(6,0)$: $36+6u=0\Rightarrow u=-6$. From $(0,8)$: $64+8v=0\Rightarrow v=-8$. So $(x-3)^{2}+(y-4)^{2}=25$; centre $(3,4)$, radius $5$. (ii) Radius to $(0,8)$ has gradient $\frac{8-4}{0-3}=-\frac43$, so tangent gradient is $\frac34$. Tangent: $y-8=\frac34 x$, i.e. $y=\frac34 x+8$. (iii) Meets x-axis at $y=0$: $\frac34 x+8=0\Rightarrow x=-\frac{32}{3}$. Point $(-\frac{32}{3},0)$. (iv) $(6-3)^{2}+(8-4)^{2}=9+16=25$, so $(6,8)$ lies on the circle.
hints: Use the general circle equation with zero constant term.
The tangent is perpendicular to the radius.
